proposition: When implementation generation is abundant, the effective bottleneck may move toward producing changes that simultaneously satisfy intent, task semantics, repository constraints, and independently specified acceptance criteria.
standard: CANDIDATE_HYPOTHESIS requires a repeated bounded pattern consistent with the proposition and at least one discriminating instance, while retaining plausible rival explanations. SUPPORTED_WITHIN_BOUNDED_COHORT would additionally require prospectively measured generation abundance, comparable opportunities, valid non-post-hoc gates, and evidence that multi-constraint satisfaction—not harness, environment, substrate, or stopping policy—controls yield.
observed_basis: All three runs produced code artifacts but zero accepted T1 states.
The controlling boundaries differed: Run 1 ordinary repository validity, Run 2 a later-audited harness mismatch, and Run 3 prospectively entailed task semantics.
Run 2 demonstrates ordinary repository PASS does not entail task acceptance; Run 1 demonstrates focused PASS does not entail repository validity.
why_not_stronger: Generation abundance was not operationalized or measured; one initial candidate per run and only two total permitted repairs were observed.
Runs are heterogeneous in objective, gate, repair, environment, and protocol maturity.
Run 2's controlling failure was harness mismatch rather than failure to satisfy a legitimate task contract.
All runs use one research repository, and no human, model, repository, or unconstrained baseline exists.
Stopping rules censor the probability of eventual acceptance.
generalization_boundary: The status describes only these three Issue #109 runs and is not evidence of a general engineering law or proof of Issue #110.
